new_scholarship.name: General Entrance Award program (GEA)
new_scholarship.funding_type: Entrance scholarship and bursary (mixed merit, leadership, involvement and financial need)
new_scholarship.duration: Awards may be one-time, or renewable for up to 4 years. Dalhousie states the yearly value range of entrance awards is "$1K to $80K" and that awards can run "over 4 years"; named international awards on the page are expressed as e.g. "$22,000 renewable for 4 years".
new_scholarship.deadline: February 15. Dalhousie states: "The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program opens on October 1, 2026, with an application deadline of February 15, 2027." The Info for International Students page repeats this for international undergraduates: "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15."
new_scholarship.application_period: The 2027-2028 GEA cycle opened on October 1, 2026 and closes at its application deadline of February 15, 2027. Dalhousie reviews applications after the February 15 deadline and notifies successful applicants in the spring. A separate early-entrance route exists with an earlier acceptance date: early entrance award offers must be accepted by paying the admission deposit by January 31.
new_scholarship.application_method: One application for the whole programme. The applicant completes the General Entrance Award application through the Dalhousie application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/ after submitting (or alongside) the undergraduate admission application. If not yet accepted, the applicant must also apply to an undergraduate programme, complete the GEA application, pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee, and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. Financial or disability-related supporting documents are uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal. Award decisions are based on Grade 12 first-semester final grades, which the school or issuing institution must send directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca to be considered official.
new_scholarship.description: Dalhousie University publishes a single undergraduate entrance award programme, the General Entrance Award program (GEA), through which international students are considered for entrance scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit/need awards. Dalhousie offers "more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year" with an approximate yearly value range of "$1K to $80K", awardable one-time or renewable for up to four years. One GEA application puts a student forward for hundreds of awards, assessed on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, with each student assessed individually on the full application. Eligibility is explicitly open to international students: "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply." Applicants must be entering directly from high school (or be a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study), be starting in the Fall term, and meet the academic requirement, typically an 80% average or 26 predicted/anticipated IB points. Named international awards listed on the page include the CorpFinance International Limited (Kevin Andrews) Indian Scholarship ($15,000, Bachelor of Commerce, students from India), the Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship ($88,000, $22,000 renewable for 4 years, Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering, students from Jamaica, academic standing and financial need) and the international strand of the Sankofa Scholarships ($48,000, $12,000 per year renewable for 4 years, international student of Black/African descent from the Caribbean entering an undergraduate degree program). Awards are not a tuition waiver: they are applied to the student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and any residual after tuition and fees may be refunded.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International students applying to Dalhousie directly from high school, or mature students with no transferable post-secondary study, who are starting in the Fall term and can supply Grade 12 first-semester final grades by the February 15 deadline. Also suitable for students whose admission route requires them to pay the $70 CAD application fee as part of the award application. Not suitable for transfer students with post-secondary study already completed, and not suitable for Winter or Summer entry, for which Dalhousie directs students to current student awards and bursaries instead.
new_scholarship.funding_period: One-time, or renewable for up to 4 years.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to all students, domestic and international. The applicant must be applying directly from high school or be a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study, must be starting in the Fall term, and must meet the academic requirement, typically an 80% average or 26 predicted/anticipated IB points, calculated using the five courses required for the programme applied for. Award decisions rest on Grade 12 first-semester final grades; later grades are not used to reassess. Applicants need not be eligible for financial aid or student loans, because many awards rest on merit or involvement. Gap year students may apply provided they have not completed transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, with an exception for Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship. Award-specific restrictions apply on top of the general rules: several named awards are limited by nationality (India, Jamaica, Caribbean heritage) or by programme (Bachelor of Commerce, Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Computer Science) and some require need.

new_scholarship.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly because the assigned award name does not exist as published. The assigned target was 'Dalhousie University International Scholarships'. No award of that name appears on dal.ca. Dalhousie does not publish a standalone international scholarship; it publishes one undergraduate entrance award programme, the General Entrance Award program (GEA), through which international students are considered for entrance scholarships and bursaries, and a parallel, separately published page for graduate international scholarships under the Faculty of Graduate Studies. The international-students page routes graduate applicants to that Faculty of Graduate Studies page and undergraduate applicants to financial aid for undergraduates, which is the separation that confirms this record's bachelor's level. This record therefore covers the GEA as the only broad international undergraduate funding instrument Dalhousie publishes. funding_amount is null on purpose: Dalhousie publishes a range, "$1K to $80K approximate range of award values yearly, and over 4 years", and per-award values rather than one programme amount, so no single CAD figure is claimed. Several named awards on the same page are restricted to Canadian high school graduates or Canadian citizens and are excluded from eligibility for an international applicant: Schulich Leader Scholarships (already indexed separately as id 312), Harrison McCain Scholarships (Canadian citizens or permanent residents), Bissett Scholarship (Cole Harbour High School), Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships and the Bachelor of Computer Science entrance scholarships (direct from high school, with the Leacross Women in Technology Scholarship the exception, which is open to Canadian and international applicants). Awards are credits against the student account, not a tuition waiver; tuition stays payable and the International Tuition Guarantee only fixes the fee at a guaranteed level. Contacts are drawn from the pages fetched, not guessed.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship, residency or international-status test is published for the programme as a whole. Dalhousie states flatly that "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply", and instructs international students to consider entrance awards "by submitting the General Entrance Award application". Individual named awards carry their own residency or nationality conditions, and several awards listed elsewhere on the same page are restricted to Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Canadian high school graduates and so are closed to an international applicant.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Confirmed directly and explicitly. The Info for International Students page states that "Dalhousie offers more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year, including scholarships and bursaries to support incoming students", that "Awards may be offered based on academics, achievements and involvement outside of the classroom, financial need or a combination of the above", and that "A general entrance award application is required to be considered". Its step-by-step international undergraduate pathway includes step 3, "Apply for scholarships: Take advantage of funding opportunities to support your studies by submitting your application for General Entrance Awards (GEA) through your Application Portal", with the note "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15." The Future undergraduate student awards page carries a dedicated "International students" section: "International students are considered for entrance awards by submitting the General Entrance Award application." International-specific documents are also addressed: a non-Canadian curriculum still requires Grade 12 first-semester marks, and where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, official government tax or income documents from the home country showing parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, are accepted, with an English translation required if not in English or French. Several awards on the page are explicitly open only to Canadian students and do not reach an international applicant: Schulich Leader Scholarships (Canadian high school or CEGEP graduate and Canadian citizen), Harrison McCain Scholarships (Canadian citizens or permanent residents) and the Bissett Scholarship (Cole Harbour High School applicants). The Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship is explicitly open to "Canadian and international applicants".
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time enrolment required to be paid: the award is applied only in the terms in which the student is "registered full-time (minimum 9 credit hours per term for degree students and 6 credit hours per term for technology students) at Dalhousie University for the term(s) in which the scholarship is awarded". The page publishes no part-time award route for the GEA programme.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field or subject restriction at programme level: one GEA application considers the applicant across faculties and programmes. Named awards are programme-restricted, including Bachelor of Commerce (CorpFinance Indian Scholarship), Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering (Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship), Bachelor of Computer Science and Bachelor of Applied Computer Science (WeAreAllCS awards, Bachelor of Computer Science entrance scholarships, Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship), Bachelor of Commerce and Bachelor of Management (Faculty of Management Promise Scholarship for Black and Indigenous Students), Music and Theatre (Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships), and Architecture & Planning, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Health and Management (Bissett Scholarship, which is also restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants). Athletic scholarships are handled separately by Dalhousie Athletics via a prospective recruit form or direct contact with a coach. The International Tuition Guarantee, which fixes rather than funds tuition, covers only the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science.
programme_detail_official.application_method: One General Entrance Award application, submitted by the applicant through the Dalhousie application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/ after the admission application. If already accepted: complete the GEA application in the portal and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. If not yet accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme, complete the GEA application, pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee, and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. Applicants admitted on self-reported grades must additionally submit an official record of first-semester results. Financial or disability-related supporting documents are uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal.

programme_detail_official.description: Dalhousie University's General Entrance Award program (GEA) is the single undergraduate entrance award route through which international students are considered for scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit-and-need awards, and one of the 2,000+ entrance awards offered annually at an approximate yearly value range of $1K to $80K, one-time or renewable for up to 4 years. One application places the applicant in the pool for hundreds of awards, assessed individually on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, on the basis of Grade 12 first-semester final grades. Eligibility is open to domestic and international students alike, requires applying directly from high school or being a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study, requires Fall entry and the usual academic threshold, and excludes transfer students. The published cycle opened on October 1, 2026 and closes February 15, 2027. Awards are credited to the student account in two instalments in mid-August and mid-December against tuition and fees, with any residual refundable; tuition is not waived, there is no bond, and living, travel and immigration costs are not covered as published components.
programme_detail_official.coverage: A monetary award credit applied to the student account against tuition and fees in two equal instalments (mid-August, mid-December), one-time or renewable for up to 4 years, with residual funds over tuition and fees refundable. Not covered: any tuition waiver, a guaranteed living-cost component, residence and meal plan costs beyond residual credit, travel, study permit, eTA, visa and Provincial Attestation Letter costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are starting in the Fall term. Winter and Summer entry cannot use the GEA route; Dalhousie directs those students to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead.

Confirm you are applying directly from high school, or that you qualify as a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship.
Check the cycle is live: the 2027-2028 GEA program opened October 1, 2026 and the deadline is February 15, 2027.
Have your Grade 12 first-semester final grades ready. If your school does not use semesters, first-half-of-year predicted or mid-term grades are acceptable.

Ask your school or issuing institution to send the transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. A transcript you upload yourself is not treated as official, and awards are not reassessed on later grades.

If your OUAC number or Nova Scotia Student ID number is already on file with Admissions you usually do not need to resend the transcript; check whether it already appears on your admission application status page, which is where transcripts are displayed, not in DalOnline.

If you have not yet been accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme and pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee as part of the award process. If you were admitted on self-reported grades, submit an official record of your first-semester results, because self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme.
Do not prepare reference letters, a resume, SAT/ACT scores or IELTS scores for the GEA application. None are required, and reference letters are not accepted for this programme.

If you need need-based support, upload financial or disability-related documents directly into the GEA application in the portal. Where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, use official government tax or income documents from your home country showing your parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, with an English translation if not in English or French.

Review which of your awards are actually open to you. Schulich Leader Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships and the Bissett Scholarship are closed to international applicants, and most separate-application awards are limited to students entering directly from Canadian high schools.

Plan the payment mechanics: the award lands on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and only registered full-time students (9 credit hours per term, 6 for technology) receive it.
If you are offered an early entrance award, be ready to pay your admission deposit by January 31 to lock it in.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the February 15 deadline. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and gives no extension, and the date is fixed regardless of when the admission application was submitted.
Applying on self-reported grades only. Dalhousie states self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme, and awards are decided on Grade 12 first-semester final grades.
Uploading your own transcript instead of having the school send it to admissions.documents@dal.ca, which means it is not considered official.
Holding transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and this cannot be waived after the fact.
Applying for Winter or Summer entry and assuming the GEA applies. Those intakes are directed to current student awards and bursaries.

Expecting IELTS or other language scores to improve the award outcome. The GEA application uses only the information in the GEA application, and IELTS scores are neither required nor considered for it.

Assuming an award title on a third-party listing is open to international applicants. Schulich Leader Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships and the Bissett Scholarship all carry Canadian residency or school conditions.
Dropping below full-time enrolment. The award is only applied in terms in which you are registered full-time, so a lighter course load silently stops the payment.
Assuming the award waives tuition. It does not: the credit is applied against tuition and fees and the fee stays payable, so a shortfall against the full international fee is still yours to cover.
Double-counting a GEA alongside an Early Entrance Scholarship. Dalhousie keeps the higher-value award only.

Deferring admission without checking the rules. Deferral is limited to the winter term and requires an approved admission deferral, and completing transferable post-secondary study during the deferred year forfeits eligibility to re-apply.
Planning around a specific award amount. Dalhousie publishes only a $1K to $80K approximate range across 2,000+ awards, so no named amount should be relied on in a funding plan.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The tuition fee itself. Awards are credits applied to the student account, not a waiver, so the full international tuition fee remains payable and must be met by the award plus other funds. Dalhousie's International Tuition Guarantee fixes and guarantees the fee for the standard programme length rather than covering it, and only for the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science. No tuition figure is recorded here because the tuition and fee calculator and tuition page were not fetched for this record.

Room and board. Residence is a separate charge and the page publishes no housing component of the award. An award that exceeds tuition and fees leaves a residual that is refunded, but that depends on the award size and is not a guaranteed living-cost amount.
Provincial Attestation Letter, study permit, Temporary Resident Visa and eTA fees for international students, none of which is listed as an award benefit.
Books, equipment and course materials. Dalhousie itself points students with urgent textbook costs toward an emergency loan, which indicates these costs are normally self-funded.
Travel to and from Halifax, or Truro, Canada, in both directions.

Health insurance, which for non-Canadian students holding a study permit is a condition of the permit and is a separate compulsory cost. No figure is recorded because the international student support pages were not fetched.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost over the degree, which no entrance award addresses.
document_audit: Official first-semester transcript sent directly by the school or issuing institution to admissions.documents@dal.ca, or a provincial student ID number for Nova Scotia and Ontario applicants. This is the single most common document failure point.
Completed General Entrance Award application, submitted by yourself through the application portal. References send nothing; reference letters are not accepted for this programme.
Financial or disability-related supporting documents uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal, where need-based or disability-specific awards require them.
For a non-Canadian curriculum that does not use semesters, first-half-of-year predicted or mid-term grades in place of first-semester final grades.

Where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, official government tax or income documents from your home country showing parent or guardian income, or an official letter from the parent or guardian's employer confirming income, with an English translation if the document is in a language other than English or French.
Nothing to prepare for reference letters, resume, SAT/ACT or IELTS; none are required for the GEA programme.

If you applied through OUAC or with a Nova Scotia Student ID number, confirm your number or transcript is showing on your admission application status page rather than resubmitting it; transcripts are added to student files manually and can take a few business days.
Confirm the record of your first-semester results actually reaches Admissions if you were admitted on self-reported grades, since self-reported grades alone disqualify you from the GEA programme.
This checklist reflects the official pages fetched; awards with their own separate-application instructions may require additional documents, and those instructions were not read for this record.

alerts.message: The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program closed its window on February 15, 2027. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and notifies successful applicants in the spring, so a late application cannot be salvaged by an earlier admission submission.

If you were admitted using self-reported grades, Dalhousie states applications with self-reported grades alone will not be considered for the General Entrance Award program. You must submit an official record of your first-semester results.

Transfer students are generally not eligible for entrance awards, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship. Holding transferable post-secondary study also ends any eligibility to re-apply after deferring.
The GEA route is Fall entry only. Students starting in winter or summer are directed to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead, which are a different pool with different terms.

Funds are applied only in terms in which you are registered full-time, a minimum of 9 credit hours per term for degree students or 6 credit hours per term for technology students. Reducing your course load silently stops the award for that term.

alerts.trigger: An award title that looks international but is not
alerts.message: Schulich Leader Scholarships require a Canadian high school or CEGEP graduation and Canadian citizenship, Harrison McCain Scholarships require Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, and the Bissett Scholarship is restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants. Check the eligibility line on each award before planning around it.

This is an account credit against tuition and fees, not a fee waiver, and the International Tuition Guarantee only fixes the fee at a guaranteed level for six named faculties. Budget the full international fee and treat the award as an offset.

If you hold both a General Entrance Award and an Early Entrance Scholarship, Dalhousie keeps only the higher-value award. Early offers must be accepted by paying the admission deposit by January 31, and that guarantees no less than the early award amount.

alerts.trigger: Timing pressure after the award offer
alerts.message: After paying the admission deposit you receive a Provincial Attestation Letter that must be used for your study permit within 12 weeks. Build the immigration timeline backwards from the February 15 award deadline and the spring notification, not forwards from it.

submission_workflow: Submit your undergraduate admission application through the application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/, paying the $70 CAD admissions application fee if you have not already paid one.
Complete the General Entrance Award application yourself in the same application portal. This single application is what puts you forward for hundreds of awards.
Ask your school or issuing institution to transmit your official Grade 12 first-semester transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. Do not rely on a self-uploaded copy.

Upload any financial or disability-related supporting documents directly inside the GEA application in the portal, and use home-country government income documents or an employer letter with an English translation if you have no Income Tax Notice of Assessment.
Verify everything is in before the February 15, 2027 deadline: Dalhousie states you must complete the application and submit all required documents before the deadline, and reviews only after it.
After the deadline, wait for notification in the spring; there is no published appeal process.
If you hold an early entrance award offer, pay your admission deposit by January 31 to guarantee no less than that early amount.
Accept your offer of admission and pay the deposit through the portal to secure the award, then expect the credit on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December.
Keep enrolment at full-time load every term the award is paid, so the 9 credit hour (or 6, technology) requirement is met and no instalment is withheld.

After the last day to add classes in each term, check whether a residual balance remains and request a refund from Student Accounts if you want the money sooner than term end; for urgent costs such as textbooks in the meantime, apply for an emergency loan.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed on both pages fetched, by explicit contrast between the undergraduate and graduate funding routes. The Future undergraduate student awards page is titled 'Future undergraduate student awards' and its scope statement is 'If you're entering Dalhousie in the fall term, you can apply for entrance awards through the General Entrance Award application', with eligibility requiring that the applicant 'Are applying directly from high school, or are a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study' and that they 'Are applying to start in the Fall term'. Every award value on the page is tied to an undergraduate degree programme, for example 'Students from India entering the Bachelor of Commerce program' and 'Students from Jamaica entering the Bachelor of Engineering program'. On the Info for International Students page the separation is explicit: a subsection headed 'For international undergraduate students' contains step 3, 'Apply for scholarships: Take advantage of funding opportunities to support your studies by submitting your application for General Entrance Awards (GEA) through your Application Portal', while graduate applicants are sent elsewhere on the same page via 'Apply for graduate scholarships, awards, and bursaries', which links to the Faculty of Graduate Studies international scholarships page. That page also states 'International students entering an undergraduate program in the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management, or Science will be part of Dalhousie's International Student Tuition Guarantee'. Bachelor's is therefore the level recorded in new_scholarship.degree_levels and programme_detail_official.degree_levels, and no master's or doctoral level is claimed for this record.
